brief: Mizuho argues agentic AI assistants (Meta's Muse, OpenAI's Dots) are accelerating demand for dedicated agentic server CPUs. Its bottom-up model has agentic CPU penetration rising from ~4% of server CPU demand in 2026E to ~30% by 2030E, taking total Server CPU TAM from ~$68B (2026E) to ~$209B by 2030E (32% CAGR), with the agentic segment itself reaching ~$80B (123% CAGR), head-node CPUs ~$68B (61% CAGR) and traditional CPUs only ~$60B (2% CAGR). The model assumes agentic-enabled MAU grows 51% CAGR and tasks per user per day grow 86% CAGR to ~21.5K by 2030E, driven by expanding agentic capability, 24/7 operation and multi-agent workflows; this also lifts DRAM and NAND shipments since agentic workloads are memory-intensive. Mizuho names ARM, AMD, INTC and NVDA as chip beneficiaries and MU/SNDK as memory beneficiaries, raising price targets on AMD ($705 from $580), SNDK ($2,050 from $1,875), DELL ($650 from $600), INTC ($114 from $92) and SMCI ($43 from $35) while reiterating existing ratings on each.
